decisions.question: How is stableFileId assigned/derived?
decisions.draftWording: 'The exact live assignment/derivation rule is OPEN; do not invent values.' (CANONICAL-IDENTITY-V1 DECISIONS point 2, 2026-09-21).
decisions.evidence: This is exactly the case the operator predicted. S01-08G (design) through S01-08I (canonical writer, commit 8bebc06741, corrected da25db92ed) resolved this fully, AFTER the draft text above was written: stableFileId = random UUIDv7, minted once on an explicit CREATE lifecycle event, never derived from path/content hash/sourceRevision/treeNodeId/packetKey/graphify_files.file_id -- matching the draft's own prohibition list exactly, just with the 'OPEN' derivation rule now closed. Verified live this pass: 5 real git commits exist (93797b4108, 8bebc06741, da25db92ed, 5f3875e69e, f8bcf9e0db), the file exists on disk, the 4 target tables (atlas_repository_identity, atlas_stable_file_identity, atlas_stable_file_revision_binding, atlas_stable_file_alias) exist live in Postgres (0 rows each, consistent with 'schema applied, population not yet authorized'). Owner census (canonicalStableFileWriterOwnerCount == 1) confirms no second writer exists. Replace the draft's 'OPEN' language with a pointer to this owner -- do not reopen this question or invent a second derivation scheme.
decisions.doesNotInvent: This reconciliation did not invent or propose a new derivation rule -- it points to the one that was already built and proven in the same tasks.md file, later in the same document.

decisions.question: Does stableFileId survive rename/move? Does delete+recreate mint a new id? Is cross-repo same-path distinct?
decisions.draftWording: Not explicitly enumerated in the original draft as a lifecycle model -- implied by 'survives content changes, workspace/source revisions and verified MOVED_PATH/HISTORICAL_PATH aliases.'
decisions.evidence: CREATE and MODIFY (same stableFileId, new revision binding) are implemented and tested (S01-08I). RENAME/alias-writing and TOMBSTONE are explicitly NOT implemented yet -- deferred to S01-08L (the 6-fixture lifecycle proof: MODIFY, RENAME, DELETE+RECREATE, CROSS-REPOSITORY-SAME-PATH, NESTED-REPOSITORY, CONCURRENT-CREATE), which is itself blocked behind the S01-08K population-apply operator token. Path-only identity resolution is structurally forbidden (sourceIdentityKey is not caller-suppliable, always computed internally as repositoryId:canonicalSourceRef). Honest split: the MODEL is decided and partially code-proven; the RENAME/TOMBSTONE fixtures are not yet empirically proven against live data. Do not treat 'rename preserves stableFileId' as proven live -- it is designed and fixture-planned, not yet run.
